headline: HSBC's head of corporate and institutional banking says AI deals are getting harder to arrange as lenders demand better returns.
score_reason: One senior banker's comment in a Bloomberg interview; supports the credit-tightening theme but is a single view.
importance_line: Companies seeking money for data centres may face tougher terms, which matters to lenders and AI builders, but this is one banker's interview and not a lending figure.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as relayed by China Daily Hong Kong, that Michael Roberts, head of corporate and institutional banking at HSBC, told Bloomberg Television that banks and investors now have "a healthy dose of skepticism" about funding the AI rollout, and that very large deals are more difficult to do. Rising interest rates and multi-decade highs in global bond yields are lifting the cost of capital, the report says.
notes: Bloomberg page blocked by a robot check; the interview coverage was read on China Daily Hong Kong and credited to Bloomberg Television.
